book.title: The Penguin Book of Independent Crosswords, volume 1

clue.text: Around Jersey, etc., distribution is easily managed

indicators.note: the dole word is placed around the islands' abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: dole is a distribution, a sharing out of money or food
Jersey and its neighbours are the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI

explanation.surface: Something about how goods are shared out around the Channel Islands being easy to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole in Britain is unemployment benefit, but here it is the older sense of a handout or share.
explanation.definitionFit: A docile person or animal is meek and compliant, so readily controlled.

clue.text: It may show expert, artistic skill — and duck's tail!

definitions.text: It may show expert, artistic skill — and duck's tail!

parts.note: a dab, or dab hand, is an expert
chic is stylish flair

indicators.note: tail means the last letter of duck's, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A display of skilful flair, finished with a duck's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a small water bird diving gracefully and showing its rear end.
explanation.definitionFit: The dabchick is the little grebe, a small diving water bird resembling a duck.

clue.text: He drives stoker overseas

definitions.meaning: first meaning: employed to drive a car
second meaning: in French ... means one who heats, a stoker

explanation.walkthrough: Early French steam cars needed a stoker, which is how the word came to mean driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is a paid driver, and the French source word literally means a heater or fireman.

clue.text: It's rich and juicy for drinker

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a heavy drinker, a drunk

explanation.walkthrough: The sentence reads as a wine review; the parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush describes luxuriant, succulent growth, and slang uses it for an alcoholic.

clue.text: Drink in clubs is a hindrance

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
hampers means impedes, is a hindrance

explanation.surface: A complaint that drinking in nightclubs gets in the way of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is informal slang for champagne, a sparkling wine.

clue.text: Privileges operating in limited periods

indicators.note: in means the word for operating goes inside the periods word

parts.note: hours are limited periods of time
on means operating, switched on

explanation.surface: Special rights that apply only during set hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Honours are distinctions or privileges conferred, as in doing someone the honour.

clue.text: Collection is requiring room in quite a few

indicators.note: in means is and the room word are placed inside the word for quite a few

parts.note: many means quite a few
a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: A collection needs room among plenty of items.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is an assortment of varied items, such as a book of mixed writings.

clue.text: It's time to get some reeling!

definitions.text: It's time to get some reeling!

parts.words: It's time to get some reeling!
parts.note: the answer is an hour on the clock, and adding 'some' gives a Scottish reel danced by a set of that many people

explanation.walkthrough: An eightsome reel is a Scottish country dance for eight dancers; 'get some' is the hint to tack on 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: The number names a clock hour, and with the suffix it names a lively Scottish dance.

clue.text: Humour having particular appeal to bore

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal, a particular kind of appeal
to tire is to bore, weary

explanation.surface: A kind of comedy that charms some people and wearies others.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is mocking humour that ridicules folly or vice.

clue.text: Imitation revolver used in grab of wages

indicators.note: used in a grab of means the gun is put inside the wages, as in a wages snatch

parts.note: pay means wages
rod is gangster slang for a gun such as a revolver

explanation.surface: A fake gun used in a payroll robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody is a mocking imitation of a style or work.

clue.text: Crew member's coil wasn't tangled round one

parts.note: a boa is a snake that kills by coiling, and a feather boa coils round the neck

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go round the numeral one
tangled means the letters of wasn't are knotted into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor's rope coil got knotted around somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' turns WASNT into TSWAN, and 'round' puts I inside that to give TSWAIN after BOA. The definition 'Crew member's' stands for 'crew member is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain is the ship's officer in charge of rigging and deck crew.

clue.text: What's the sense in having a great many?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the five senses
second meaning: informal, as in 'a ... of money', a large amount

explanation.walkthrough: The question pretends to ask what point there is in owning lots; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five faculties, and colloquially the word also means a large quantity.

clue.text: Removal from board in fit of anger

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in draughts, to ... is to remove an opponent's piece that failed to capture
second meaning: a sulky fit of pique

explanation.walkthrough: Draughts (checkers) has an old rule where a piece that misses a compulsory capture is huffed, taken off the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a huff means being in a sulk of offended irritation.

clue.text: Many employ different rate for lazy person

parts.note: a lot means many
use means employ

indicators.note: different signals that the letters of rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: Plenty of people charge a different rate for someone idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' makes ATER from RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer the lotus-eaters lived in dreamy idleness, so the term describes an indolent pleasure-seeker.

clue.text: Note dirty mess developing into power network

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: developing means the letters of dirty mess turn into a new order

explanation.surface: A message about a mess spreading through the electricity grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' makes RIDSYSTEM from DIRTYMESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The grid system is the national network of cables distributing electricity.

clue.text: Extreme members of council before their time, obviously

indicators.note: the extreme members of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Councillors at the fringes arriving prematurely, evidently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' here are letters of council, not councillors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen clearly is plainly evident, so the adverb means evidently.

clue.text: Fodder is turned before long to mature

indicators.note: turned means the word is is read backwards

parts.note: to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Animal feed is turned over well before it is left to mature.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is grass or other green crops fermented in a silo to feed livestock.

clue.text: You have to settle down to Roman life — in cage!

indicators.note: in means the Latin word sits inside the cage word

parts.note: a grate is a grid of bars, like a cage
vita is the Latin, Roman, word for life

explanation.surface: Settling into a Roman way of living, though behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To gravitate is to sink or move downward under gravity, so to come to rest.

clue.text: Obsession of EEC initially in sins in organisation

indicators.note: in means the prefix sits inside the rearranged letters
in organisation means the letters of sins are organised anew

parts.note: Euro- is the prefix, used at the start of words, for things of the EEC or Europe

explanation.surface: Fixation on European sins within some body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in organisation' makes NSIS from SINS. The EEC was the European Economic Community, forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder marked by anxiety, often an obsessive fixation.

clue.text: To obtain acknowledgement, order direct

indicators.note: to order letters is to arrange them afresh, so direct is rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to give direct orders in order to be recognised.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is recognition given for an achievement, as in film credits.

clue.text: Ground to soak up wet weather

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Land that absorbs rainfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RET into TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features.

clue.text: On tree you'll see it wrinkle with advancing years

parts.note: a line is a wrinkle on the face
age is advancing years

explanation.surface: Wrinkles appearing as you get older.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is a family tree, not a wooden one.
explanation.definitionFit: A family tree charts ancestry and descent from forebears.

clue.text: Animal is, it's said, encased in fat

indicators.note: encased in means the sound sits inside the fat word

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: it's said means the letters are spelt as the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: the word is is pronounced with a Z sound

explanation.surface: Some creature apparently wrapped in fat.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works on how 'is' is pronounced, with a Z sound, which is written into the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lizard is a scaly reptile with four legs and a long tail.

clue.text: Have a let-down, base collapsing on one left below!

indicators.note: collapsing means the letters of base fall into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Disappointment as a base caves in on someone left beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let-down' means being lowered on a rope, not a disappointment. 'collapsing' makes ABSE from BASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a rock face on a rope, being lowered down.

clue.text: Trap, of sorts, to force open for ultimate reward!

parts.note: a booby trap is one sort of trap
to prize something is to lever it open

explanation.surface: A kind of trap that must be levered open to get the final reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate' means last: the prize given to whoever finishes bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby prize is a joke award for coming last in a competition.

clue.text: Operating part stops on it

parts.note: a body part that may be operated on, and a keyboard instrument fitted with stops

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like surgery halting; it means a body part operated on, and the musical instrument with stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A liver or kidney is a bodily component, and the church instrument has stops that select its pipes.

clue.text: One's driven in through arch support

indicators.note: driven in means the numeral is hammered inside the preposition

parts.note: per means through or by means of
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pile driven down to hold up an arch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a solid pillar bearing the weight of an arch or bridge span.

clue.text: Run down to junction for 9 down

parts.note: to ski is to run down a slope
a T is a T-junction

explanation.surface: A slope run leading to a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 down is PARODY.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch imitating something, a parody.

clue.text: Work to reverse grass disease

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

indicators.note: reverse means the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: An instruction to go to work fighting a disease of the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungal infection of rye and other cereal grasses.

clue.text: I'm running a risk with a fan coming out with language!

indicators.note: coming out suggests the letters emerge jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker confessing to danger alongside an admirer who comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm running' is surface padding. The first A stays put and 'coming out' rearranges RISK A FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaans is a South African tongue descended from Dutch.

clue.text: Embrocation is nothing to upset people covered in it

indicators.note: to upset a word in an across clue is to turn it backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

indicators.note: covered in means the people word sits inside the letters of it

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: A rubbing lotion is harmless, and people get smeared in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liniment is a soothing lotion rubbed into the skin for aches.

clue.text: Force lock to get behind front of safe

indicators.note: the lock word is placed behind, after, the letter from safe
front of means the first letter of safe

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A safecracker forcing a lock to reach what is behind the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' is a lock of hair, not a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is pressure or strain, a force applied to a material.
